name: Maryland
metaDescription: Maryland insurance guides covering auto requirements, homeowners, renters, and business coverage, plus official Maryland Insurance Administration and MVA resources.
overview: Maryland requires registered vehicles to carry liability insurance, matching uninsured motorist coverage, and a personal injury protection offer. Homeowners insurance is not required by state law, though mortgage lenders typically require it. Renters insurance is generally optional unless a lease requires it. Most employers with one or more employees must carry workers' compensation insurance.
requiredInsuranceSummary: Maryland's most common legal insurance requirements are auto liability (currently 30/60/15) with matching UM/UIM, a PIP offer that can be waived in writing, and workers' compensation for nearly all employers with one or more employees. Homeowners and renters insurance are not mandated by statute.
majorRisks: Coastal and Chesapeake Bay wind and storm exposure
Flood risk in waterfront, low-lying, and inland overflow areas
Winter weather and nor'easters, especially in western and central Maryland

name: Virginia
metaDescription: Virginia insurance guides covering auto requirements, homeowners, renters, and business coverage, plus official SCC Bureau of Insurance and DMV resources.
overview: Virginia requires registered vehicles to carry 50/100/25 liability insurance and uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage at least at those statutory minimums. Extra UM/UIM may be reduced, but it cannot be dropped. The uninsured motor vehicle fee option ended July 1, 2024. Homeowners insurance is not required by statute. Workers' compensation is generally required for employers with three or more employees.
requiredInsuranceSummary: Virginia's core mandates are auto liability at 50/100/25 for policies effective January 1, 2025 or later, UM/UIM at least at those statutory minimums, and workers' compensation at three or more employees. Homeowners and renters insurance are not required by state law.
majorRisks: Higher dwelling replacement costs in Northern Virginia
Coastal exposure in Hampton Roads versus inland and mountain weather inland
Severe thunderstorms, winter storms, and localized flooding

name: Washington, D.C.
metaDescription: Washington, D.C. insurance guides covering auto requirements, homeowners, renters, and business coverage, plus official DISB and DC DMV resources.
overview: Washington, D.C. requires 25/50/10 auto liability and uninsured motorist coverage. The District has a high share of renters, rowhomes, condos, and older housing stock, so lease-required renters insurance and building-specific property coverage come up often. Most employers need workers' compensation. Homeowners insurance is not required by District statute, but lenders typically require it.
requiredInsuranceSummary: D.C. requires auto liability at 25/50/10 plus uninsured motorist coverage. PIP is generally optional. Homeowners and renters insurance are not mandated by statute, though leases and mortgages often require coverage. Most employers must carry workers' compensation.
majorRisks: Rowhomes, condos, and older housing stock
Urban property, theft, and liability exposure
